content.xhtml:p: PUMP STATION LEAD/LAG CONTROL, ladder logic version of pump_station.st. Specification: design/pump-station-design.md sections 4 (logic) and 5 (register map). Pressures are UINT scaled x10: 1200 means 120.0 psi. Rungs run top to bottom once per 100 ms scan.
1. FIRST SCAN DEFAULTS (design 4.4). %MW memory is not kept across a runtime restart, so a zero setpoint means the settings were never written.
Load the default settings
2. CLAMP HMI SETTINGS to their allowed ranges (design 5.3). The clamped value is written back, so the HMI reads back what the PLC is using. Then decode the commands into bits.
Setpoints. The lag stop pressure stays at least 10 psi above the lag start pressure.
Commands
Mode bits. Off is neither Auto nor Manual.
Lead selection and manual commands
Pressure tests used by the lead/lag and alarm rungs
3. PUMP HEALTH (design 4.2 step 4 and 4.3). Fault feedback, or no running feedback 5 s after a run command, locks the pump out until the operator presses Reset and the fault has cleared.
P1 commanded but not running
P2 commanded but not running
Lock out a pump that faults or fails to start
Reset releases a lockout once the fault has cleared
4. AUTO MODE: LEAD/LAG (design 4.1, 4.2). The lead pump always runs; the lag pump starts when pressure stays below SP_PRESSURE and stops when it stays above SP_LAG_STOP.
Entering Auto (rising edge of ModeAuto)
Entering Auto: take the operator's lead choice
Is the pump that is now lag already commanded to run?
Entering Auto: keep whatever is already running, so the switch causes no bump
Failover: the lead pump has failed and the other pump is healthy
Promote the healthy pump. The HMI lead selection follows, so the station does not swap back by itself after Reset.
Operator changed the lead pump: applied only while the lag pump is stopped (design 4.2 step 5) and the new lead is healthy
Make-before-break: the old lead keeps running (Handover) until the new lead reports running. The old lead is always the other pump, so the ST program's OldLead is not needed.
Lead and lag pump health and feedback
Handover ends when the new lead runs, or cannot run
Lag delays as TIME (OpenPLC converts an integer to TIME as seconds)
Lag start: pressure below SP_PRESSURE for LAG_START_DELAY (step 2). EN = ModeAuto: the timer only runs in Auto.
Lag stop: pressure above SP_LAG_STOP for LAG_STOP_DELAY (step 3). The gap between the two pressures is the hysteresis that stops short-cycling.
Manual and Off: no lag request, no handover
PUMP COMMANDS. Auto: the lead runs, the lag runs when called for, and the old lead runs during a handover. Manual: the operator's command. Off: stopped. A locked-out pump is never commanded.
P1 run command
P2 run command
Outside Manual the manual commands track the pumps, so switching to Manual is bumpless
5. ALARMS (design 4.3). Each alarm latches until the operator presses Reset AND its condition has cleared. Reset also acknowledges.
Low pressure is armed 15 s after leaving Off, so a normal start-up does not alarm
Low pressure for 5 s
High pressure for 5 s
Simulator comm loss: heartbeat has not changed for 3 s
Latch the alarms
Reset: clear each alarm whose condition has gone, acknowledge, and clear the reset command
A newly raised alarm is unacknowledged until the next Reset
6. STATUS FOR THE HMI, holding registers 0..7 (design 5.2)
Lag pump running feedback
Values
Status word: add each bit's value when the bit is on
Alarm word, the same way
PLC heartbeat: +1 every scan, 65535 wraps to 0
